page.layout: One page of text in one column, with no marginal notes. Page number "24" at top left. Running head "CONCIONES" at top centre. Catchword "les" at right below the last line.

main_text.p: Deus, à cuius dilectione nihil nos separare potest,

Eruntq; in carne unam) vel,in carne una: id est,officia dilectionis mutua exhibebunt. Vir igitur si diligat uxorem, carnem suam dilexerit:& eam si odiat, se oderit. Qui igitur inuisam[?] Christus sponsam suam odio habe-at? in quo typi corpus & veritas cernitur. Notandum autem quod haec verba, ἔσονται εἰ[?] δύο εἰς σάρκα μίαν (Sic.n.L X X. verterunt)in Euangelicis scriptis inueniantur ad diuersas causas translata. Primum quidem Christus ea usurpat Matt.19. ad probandum,quòd nō liceat uxorem quavis de causa, more Iudaeis recepto, repudiare,& alteram in matrimonium ducere. Haec insignis doctrina est. Ex-ijsdem verbis Apostolus ad Eph.5. ratiocinatur,arctissimam esse mariti & uxoris coniunctionem,charitatemque indissolubilem. Ubi sanè egregia institutio commendatioque est vitae coniugalis proposita. At 1. Cor. 6. colligit ex'illis verbis,eum qui scortatur, membra sua facere membra meretricis. Faciunt igitur eadem verba ad morum correctionem. Hoc autem pacto, ex quacunque historia, multiplex & varia eruditio spiritualis, ab ijs qui diligentes sunt,colligi potest.
7 Porrò de nuditate Adami & Euae in pa-radiso Moses ita loquitur: Fuerunt autem ambo illi nudi, homo, inquam, ille, & uxor eius,& non erubescebant:vel, non confusibi

page.notes: Greek line in the second paragraph: the opening word is printed with an ornamented first letter, and the word after "ἔσονται" reads as "εἰ" in the scan, where the LXX has "οἱ"; marked [?]. The Greek phrase "εἰ δύο" also needs checking against the printed original. "inuisam" is my reading of the word printed "inuifam" (or "intuifam"); marked [?]. Long s is written as plain s throughout (for example "separare", "sponsam"), and u/v is normalised as the rules require. "ex'illis" keeps the printed apostrophe. "Iudaeis" is written whole: the word is split across a line end without a printed hyphen. The last line ends on a half word ("confusibi"); the continuation "les" is the catchword.
